glintr100-antelopev2.name: glintr100 (antelopev2) [baseline]
glintr100-antelopev2.license: InsightFace model zoo: non-commercial research use
glintr100-antelopev2.notes: The reference model for the whole benchmark. Detector in the same pack (SCRFD) is not used: inputs are already aligned.

auraface-v1.name: AuraFace-v1
auraface-v1.training_data: 'commercially and publicly available data sources' (model card)
auraface-v1.pre: ONNX, RGB, (x-127.5)/127.5, 112x112 (verified identical to InsightFace's own loader)
auraface-v1.notes: Only commercially-licensed ResNet-100 tested, but scored far below the baseline on this protocol. Cause not investigated (training data vs. alignment mismatch are both possible).

w600k-r50-buffalo-l.name: w600k_r50 (buffalo_l)
w600k-r50-buffalo-l.license: InsightFace model zoo: non-commercial research use
w600k-r50-buffalo-l.notes: Recognizer of the popular buffalo_l pack.

w600k-mbf-buffalo-s.name: w600k_mbf (buffalo_s)
w600k-mbf-buffalo-s.license: InsightFace model zoo: non-commercial research use
w600k-mbf-buffalo-s.notes: Small and fast. CoreML cannot run this model, the loader falls back to CPU automatically.

sface-opencv.name: SFace (OpenCV)
sface-opencv.pre: OpenCV cv2.FaceRecognizerSF.feature() on the aligned 112x112 BGR crop (OpenCV does its own preprocessing)
sface-opencv.notes: 128-d embedding (all others are 512-d). Commercially friendly licence, mid-to-low accuracy here.

edgeface-base.name: EdgeFace-Base
edgeface-base.arch: EdgeNeXt-based hybrid CNN/Transformer with low-rank linear layers
edgeface-base.notes: Edge-device family; 18.23M params and 1398.83 MFLOPs per the model card. Code is fetched from github.com/otroshi/edgeface at run time (not vendored).

edgeface-s.name: EdgeFace-S (g=0.5)
edgeface-s.arch: EdgeNeXt-based hybrid CNN/Transformer with low-rank linear layers
edgeface-s.notes: Edge-device family; 3.65M params and 306.12 MFLOPs per the model card. Code is fetched from github.com/otroshi/edgeface at run time (not vendored).

edgeface-xs.name: EdgeFace-XS (g=0.6)
edgeface-xs.arch: EdgeNeXt-based hybrid CNN/Transformer with low-rank linear layers
edgeface-xs.notes: Edge-device family; 1.77M params and 154.00 MFLOPs per the model card. Code is fetched from github.com/otroshi/edgeface at run time (not vendored).

edgeface-xxs.name: EdgeFace-XXS
edgeface-xxs.arch: EdgeNeXt-based hybrid CNN/Transformer with low-rank linear layers
edgeface-xxs.notes: Edge-device family; 1.24M params and 94.72 MFLOPs per the model card. Code is fetched from github.com/otroshi/edgeface at run time (not vendored).

vit-tiny8-arcface-gaunernst.name: ViT-Tiny/8 ArcFace (gaunernst)
vit-tiny8-arcface-gaunernst.license: not stated on the model card
vit-tiny8-arcface-gaunernst.pre: timm, RGB, mean/std 0.5 from the model's pretrained_cfg, 112x112
vit-tiny8-arcface-gaunernst.notes: Tiny ViT, ~5.5M params. Output is not normalised by the model: the harness L2-normalises.

vit-tiny8-adaface-gaunernst.name: ViT-Tiny/8 AdaFace (gaunernst)
vit-tiny8-adaface-gaunernst.license: not stated on the model card

vit-tiny8-adaface-gaunernst.notes: Tiny ViT, ~5.5M params. Output is not normalised by the model: the harness L2-normalises.

adaface-ir101-webface12m.license: model card: 'follow the license of the training dataset'
adaface-ir101-webface12m.notes: Needs transformers==4.44.2, fvcore, omegaconf, einops. Run in its own process (CVLface models share a `models` package name).

adaface-ir50-ms1mv2.license: model card: 'follow the license of the training dataset'
adaface-ir50-ms1mv2.notes: Needs transformers==4.44.2, fvcore, omegaconf, einops. Run in its own process (CVLface models share a `models` package name).

facenet-casia-webface.name: FaceNet InceptionResNetV1 (CASIA-WebFace)
facenet-casia-webface.license: code MIT (facenet-pytorch); weights terms follow training data
facenet-casia-webface.pre: PyTorch, RGB, (x-127.5)/128 at 160x160 (our 112x112 crops are bilinearly upsampled)
facenet-casia-webface.notes: Understated: FaceNet expects looser 160x160 crops than these tight 112x112 ones. Clean score (not trained on VGGFace2).

facenet-vggface2-leaked.name: FaceNet InceptionResNetV1 (VGGFace2) [LEAKED]
facenet-vggface2-leaked.training_data: VGGFace2 = the same data as this benchmark (LEAKED, not a fair score)
facenet-vggface2-leaked.license: code MIT (facenet-pytorch); weights terms follow training data
facenet-vggface2-leaked.notes: LEAKED: trained on VGGFace2, so this score is inflated and must not be compared with the others. Shown for completeness only.

clip-vit-l14.key: CLIP ViT-L/14 image encoder (LLaVA vision-tower family)
clip-vit-l14.name: CLIP ViT-L/14 image encoder
clip-vit-l14.arch: ViT-L/14 image tower (the vision-encoder family used by LLaVA)
clip-vit-l14.training_data: web image-text pairs (general purpose, not face-specific)
clip-vit-l14.notes: Included to test the 'general-purpose encoder' claim: far below face-specific models.

lvface-t.name: LVFace-T (Glint360K)
lvface-t.training_data: Glint360K (same data as the antelopev2 baseline)
lvface-t.license: model card + code: MIT. The licence file covers the code; weights / Glint360K terms NOT verified
lvface-t.notes: CoreML cannot run the ViT layers, so on Apple Silicon this runs on CPU (slow for -B). LVFace-L was run separately through the official PyTorch code on the GPU (see the lvface-l folder).

lvface-s.name: LVFace-S (Glint360K)
lvface-s.training_data: Glint360K (same data as the antelopev2 baseline)
lvface-s.license: model card + code: MIT. The licence file covers the code; weights / Glint360K terms NOT verified
lvface-s.notes: CoreML cannot run the ViT layers, so on Apple Silicon this runs on CPU (slow for -B). LVFace-L was run separately through the official PyTorch code on the GPU (see the lvface-l folder).

lvface-b.name: LVFace-B (Glint360K)
lvface-b.training_data: Glint360K (same data as the antelopev2 baseline)
lvface-b.license: model card + code: MIT. The licence file covers the code; weights / Glint360K terms NOT verified
lvface-b.notes: CoreML cannot run the ViT layers, so on Apple Silicon this runs on CPU (slow for -B). LVFace-L was run separately through the official PyTorch code on the GPU (see the lvface-l folder).

lvface-l.name: LVFace-L (Glint360K)
lvface-l.arch: Vision Transformer (ViT-L, patch 9), progressive cluster optimisation (ICCV 2025)
lvface-l.training_data: Glint360K (same data as the antelopev2 baseline)
lvface-l.license: model card + code: MIT. The licence file covers the code; weights / Glint360K terms NOT verified
lvface-l.notes: Run through the official PyTorch code on the GPU (MPS) because the ONNX build runs on CPU and takes hours. The PyTorch loader was cross-checked against the ONNX model (cosine similarity of embeddings on 64 images).

magface-r100-ms1mv2.name: MagFace iResNet-100 (MS1MV2)
magface-r100-ms1mv2.license: Apache-2.0 (repo); trained on MS1MV2, whose dataset terms apply
magface-r100-ms1mv2.pre: PyTorch, BGR, x/255 with no mean/std (as in the MagFace repo), 112x112
magface-r100-ms1mv2.notes: Only the direction of the embedding is used (its norm is a quality score). Listed on the IJB-C leaderboard as MagFace+ (95.97).

elasticface-cosplus-ms1mv2.name: ElasticFace-Cos+ iResNet-100 (MS1MV2)
elasticface-cosplus-ms1mv2.notes: Listed on the IJB-C leaderboard (96.65). Architecture is the standard arcface_torch iResNet-100.

lafs-part-fvit-wf4m.name: LAFS Part-fViT (WebFace4M)
lafs-part-fvit-wf4m.license: MIT (repo); trained on WebFace4M, whose dataset terms apply
lafs-part-fvit-wf4m.pre: PyTorch, RGB, x/255 - 0.5 (no division, as in the repo's IJB evaluation), 112x112
lafs-part-fvit-wf4m.notes: Supervised Part-fViT without LAFS pre-training (README: IJB-C TAR@FAR=1e-4 97.40). Needs ipython, einops, timm. The checkpoint also holds the training classification head.

lafs-part-fvit-wf4m-lafs.name: LAFS Part-fViT (WebFace4M, LAFS pre-trained)
lafs-part-fvit-wf4m-lafs.license: MIT (repo); trained on WebFace4M, whose dataset terms apply
lafs-part-fvit-wf4m-lafs.pre: PyTorch, RGB, x/255 - 0.5 (no division, as in the repo's IJB evaluation), 112x112
lafs-part-fvit-wf4m-lafs.notes: With LAFS self-supervised pre-training (README: IJB-C 97.58; the leaderboard lists LAFS at 97.48). Needs ipython, einops, timm. The checkpoint also holds the training classification head.

vit8r-vitb-wf4m.name: ViT-8R: ViT-Base with 8 registers (WebFace4M)
vit8r-vitb-wf4m.arch: Vision Transformer Base (patch 9) with 8 register tokens
vit8r-vitb-wf4m.notes: Appears on the IJB-C leaderboard as ViT-8R (97.37). Weights are hosted on a Fraunhofer OwnCloud share (it returned HTTP 503 for a while on first try). The repo README gives no usage code: the model is built with the repo's get_model('vit_b', num_register_token=8) and the checkpoint loads with zero missing / unexpected keys.
